_comment: Declarative model routing for Agent OS. This is the spec that stage 4 enforces.
Each tab talks to its own model. There is no shared pipeline.
Read this before changing any model anywhere. Hand this to an AI agent instead of
letting it guess, because the common failure is an assistant 'tidying up' by pointing

never_use.why: Labs release these free for a few weeks to collect data, then remove them or start charging. Your setup breaks with no warning and no error you can act on. Always use a named :free model instead.

inheritance: Jarvis runs on top of Hermes, so Jarvis is only ever as smart as Hermes' model.
Subagents inherit the model of whatever spawned them.

jobs.label: Free on-device building (Agent Factory, Game Studio, Agent Kanban)
jobs.note: gemma2 is better at animation and generative art. qwen2.5-coder is sharper at full apps. Same local speed, so pick by job.

jobs.label: Free Claude Code and coding subagents

deny_reason.http_402: Your free model was retired. Swap to a current named :free model.
deny_reason.http_429: OpenRouter free cap is 50 requests/day with no credit. Add $5 once to raise it to 1,000/day, or switch to local for unlimited.

jobs.label: Hermes, and therefore Jarvis, Loop, Goal Mode, Radar, Mastermind
jobs.why_deny: Small local models cannot drive the Hermes tool loop. You get an agent that looks like it is working and silently does nothing.

jobs.label: Claude tab
jobs.auth: claude login (browser OAuth, uses your Claude plan)
jobs.note: Opus 4.8 is lighter on plan tokens. Fable 5 is stronger on the hardest jobs and roughly double the cost.
jobs.trap: Never set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. An EMPTY value in a .env.local silently overrides your login and breaks the tab. This is the single most common Claude tab failure.

jobs.label: Video Studio Create, OpenMontage
jobs.why: The renderer renders whatever composition the model authors. A small model produces five-second colour blobs and people blame the renderer.

jobs.label: DeepSeek Coder, Muse Code, jcode, Prime Agent, GPT 5.6 Code
jobs.note: Each of these is its own tab with its own brain. They do NOT share a model with Hermes or with the local builder. Setting one does not set the others.
jobs.why_deny: These tabs drive multi-step build loops. A small local model cannot complete them and fails in ways that look like the tab is broken.

policy._comment: One rule to follow when picking a brain for a job.
policy.everyday_web_app: GPT 5.6 Code, or GLM-5.2 if you want it cheaper
policy.second_opinion: run the same prompt through Kimi or Qwen and compare
